method: Read-only exact Git blobs and targeted diff; no compilation, tests, benchmarks, Host qualification or ref changes.

inputs.review_scope: changed verify path and original full function
new 46-line scoped control plus surrounding original current-account controls
new SQL commit observation block and observation integration
new observation controls and unchanged surrounding original assertions
State alias and immutable map representation only

conclusion: No confirmed blocker in the inspected scoped account-projection reuse or SQL observation implementation. This is static review only.
findings: State is the concrete BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>. CurrentAccounts borrows that exact State, stores parsed values in private fields, and values_for requires pointer identity. The borrow excludes ordinary mutable access during its lifetime; no persisted scope or retained ArithmeticCache stores the projection.

Only fresh complete-state parsing supplies CurrentAccounts after the original state/account roots, count, aggregate and conservation computation. An absent/foreign projection follows the original account parser.

verify_state_with_readback still checks the current scope, loads/verifies the record, compares complete commitment, reads current SQL graph through the existing original or sealed scoped path, preserves original progress checkpoints, rechecks scope/frontier after the final callback, and falls back to ordinary verification on invalidated reuse.

The new projection changes parsing reuse, not the existing certified-frontier rules. A preexisting frontier may already omit certified descendants; do not describe every scoped call as a full SQL graph walk. Without that existing certification the original traversal remains.

The added cold scoped control uses two fresh caches under the same real writer, discards only the projection for the control, compares outcome/checkpoint parity, expects one versus two parses, rolls back and checks total_changes. It is not evidence that all foreign-state or late-error controls were newly executed.

SqlCommitObservation uses short try_lock operations and holds no mutex across Transaction::commit. Result observation records success/failure without replacing the original result. Unknown CPU stays unknown; accounting overflow/contention marks observation_failed. Observation fields carry no consensus authority.
boundaries: SQL observation can lose a completion update on contention: calls_in_flight may then remain nonzero, with observation_failed true. Do not treat that telemetry as a precise live-transaction inventory.
Timing includes observation overhead and the Transaction::commit API's error/drop behavior; it is not isolated SQL statement time or a physical-fsync measurement.
Store/reorg caller changes are owned by the Chain agent and are outside this review's full-source claim.
No native or original Host/performance result is transferred from 056, 312 or any earlier source.
